items.headline: Stocks bounced back as money rotated out of AI and chip names
items.note: On Thursday the Dow rose about 1.1% to 52,177.69 and the S&P 500 gained about 0.3%, while the Nasdaq finished roughly flat. Investors moved into cheaper, less rate-sensitive stocks as Treasury yields fell and bank earnings helped.

items.headline: TSMC posts record profit, but its stock still fell
items.note: Net profit rose 69% to T$763.1 billion, its sixth straight record quarter, and Q4 revenue guidance is $52.3-54.3 billion. The stock slipped because the CEO sounded more cautious about 2027 and said the cycle "won't go forever", a read-through for AI demand.

items.headline: Chip stocks extend their losing streak despite strong AI demand
items.note: The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 0.9%, its seventh straight losing session, and Nvidia dropped 1.8%. Worries about how the AI buildout is financed are weighing on the sector you want to work in.

items.headline: Hot inflation data keeps more Fed rate hikes in play
items.note: Wednesday's hotter-than-expected consumer inflation was followed by a hot producer price report, and one bank (UBS) now expects a third Fed hike. Higher rates raise borrowing costs for AI companies and startups.

items.headline: September jobs report was weak: only 29,000 jobs added
items.note: Economists expected 90,000, and unemployment rose to 4.2%. A soft labor market makes the entry-level search more competitive, though it also lowered the odds of a Fed hike in October.

learn.explain: A bond is a loan you make to a government or company: they pay you regular interest and return your money at the end. The yield is the return you earn as a percentage of the bond's current price. When a bond's price goes up, its yield goes down, and the other way around. Investors buy safer bonds when they want shelter from stock swings, which pushes prices up and yields down. Today's example: on Thursday Treasury yields fell as investors moved out of AI stocks, and that helped the market bounce back.
learn.try: Look up the current 10-year Treasury yield and see how it has moved this month.
